candidate: <full commit hash of the pull request head being merged>
tasks: <T-NNNN of every task this candidate delivers>

verification.environment: <where the implementer checks ran: runner, OS, runtime versions>

checks.name: <required check name exactly as CI reports it>
checks.result: <passed | failed | skipped, as observed; under approval.auto_merge a required check GitHub enforces before merge may be enforced, with the pull request's checks page as its reference>
checks.reference: <https link to the CI run or log for this commit>

execution.run: <https link to the run that passed the tests listed in passed>

<test file mapped in tests/acceptance-ma: <name of each passing test in it, as mapped>

tests.file: <only a mapped test that did not pass: its file>
tests.name: <its name, as mapped>

integration.revision: <the same full commit hash, assembled with the current trusted branch>

checks.name: <required check name exactly as CI reports it>
checks.result: <passed | failed | skipped, as observed; under approval.auto_merge a required check GitHub enforces before merge may be enforced, with the pull request's checks page as its reference>
checks.reference: <https link to the CI run for this commit>

review.implementer: <the tasks' owner, as recorded in the task records>
review.vendor: <the maker of the reviewer's model, e.g. OpenAI or Google>
review.fixes_after: <only when the review is of an earlier revision and the code changed after it: { "tests": [the tests that failed without each blocking fix] }; otherwise leave this field out>
review.fix_check: <only after a blocking finding at deep: { "candidate", "reviewer", "model", "vendor", "report" } of the fix check of this candidate; otherwise leave this field out>
review.fallback: <only when a deep review could not use review.second_model: why; otherwise leave this field out>

context.provider: <harness that launched the review, e.g. the tool and its subagent feature>
context.candidate: <the same full commit hash the reviewer inspected>
context.launch_evidence: <https link to where the launch prompt and context identifier are posted>

coverage: <each area reviewed: scope, correctness, maintainability, security, regression, test-fidelity>

findings.resolution: <how it was resolved, with the commit>
findings.exposure: <for a blocking, critical or high finding: what it exposes, to whom; leave out otherwise>
findings.carried_by: <only for a blocking finding a found task fixes (procedures/review.md): its T-NNNN; otherwise leave out this and the next two>
paths: <the files or folders of its code, none changed here>
findings.merge_increases_exposure: <false: the merge does not increase its exposure>

tasks: <T-NNNN of every task the review covered>
review.report: <https link to the posted review report (templates/review.md)>
